topic: Family Law — Variation of Maintenance Order
user_query: I lost my job and cannot afford to pay my ex-wife maintenance.
variations: Can I lower the maintenance amount?
Apply to change court order for maintenance
My expenses went up, need to pay less
Ex-husband earning more, want to increase maintenance
part_a_general_info: You can apply to the Family Justice Courts to vary (change) an existing maintenance order if you can prove a material change in circumstances (e.g., retrenchment, serious illness, or significant change in the child's expenses). You cannot simply stop paying; you must continue paying the ordered amount until the court changes it, otherwise you face enforcement action. Variation applications can be made by either party — whether seeking a reduction or an increase.
triage_questions: Q1: Is there an existing court order?
Q2: What is the 'material change'? (e.g., lost job, pay cut, remarriage)
Q3: Do you have documents to prove this change (e.g., retrenchment letter)?
Q4: Are you currently in arrears (owe money)?
branching_logic: If Q4 = Yes (in arrears) → Warn that enforcement proceedings may happen concurrently with the variation application.
routing: Route A (Standard variation): Apply for variation at Family Justice Courts (FJC) or via iFAMS online.
Route B (Needs help with application): Refer to PBSG Family Law Clinic or Legal Aid Bureau (if eligible).
guardrail: Must NOT predict whether the court will accept the specific reason for variation.
